target.transport: native USB composite CDC and HID mouse, plus authenticated Wi-Fi OTA when ignored credentials are present
target.current_device_policy: Before flashing a StickS3 used by another project, identify its serial port and preserve the complete flash under ignored .device-backups. The tested unit has a verified recovery image. OTA must resolve sticks3-ptt.local and match the saved AC:27:6E:D2:68:B8 hardware MAC; bedside-countdown-s3 is a separate device and must never be targeted.

validated_facts.fact: The internal IMU is a BMI270 at I2C address 0x68 on SDA GPIO47 and SCL GPIO48.
validated_facts.validation: M5Stack StickS3 documentation and M5Unified StickS3 board implementation

validated_facts.fact: The internal infrared transmitter is GPIO46 and the infrared receiver is GPIO42.
The infrared receiver is a demodulating digital receiver intended for RMT pulse capture, not an analog reflectance channel.
validated_facts.validation: M5Stack documents RMT-only reception and its remote-control distance guidance; this makes blink sensing unproven until measured.

validated_facts.fact: The internal IR path needs the controlled external 5 V output and must not be enabled while an external source drives that rail.
validated_facts.validation: M5Stack StickS3 power and IR documentation; firmware defaults the rail off and requires a physical two-second hold.

validated_facts.fact: USB HID on ESP32-S3 requires TinyUSB native mode ARDUINO_USB_MODE=0; ARDUINO_USB_MODE=1 selects hardware USB-JTAG CDC and cannot run USBHIDMouse.
validated_facts.validation: Espressif Arduino core 2.0.17 and 3.x USB examples, installed core sources, and Context7 official-source excerpts

validated_facts.fact: Wokwi can execute a generic ESP32-S3 DevKitC firmware image, but its documented board list does not provide a complete StickS3 model.
validated_facts.validation: Official Wokwi ESP32 guide, Wokwi CLI documentation, Context7 Wokwi documentation index, and a successful Wokwi CLI run of the cross-compiled simulator harness

validated_facts.fact: No public tool currently provides a complete StickS3 emulator.
validated_facts.validation: M5Stack lv_m5_emulator is a native SDL UI tool whose current targets omit StickS3; UiFlow2 runs programs on a connected device; Espressif QEMU covers the ESP32-S3 SoC only; Wokwi exposes a generic ESP32-S3 rather than the complete board.

validated_facts.fact: The tested StickS3 enumerates as a native TinyUSB composite CDC and HID mouse, initializes its BMI270, accepts the large blue Button A, and moves the host pointer from head motion while mounted on glasses.
validated_facts.validation: Physical 2026-08-14 bench and worn-device tests; a stationary armed control produced zero host input events before the worn pointer test.

validated_facts.fact: The integrated IR pair is not a viable near-eye reflectance sensor in the tested geometry.
validated_facts.validation: Multiple physical tests produced inseparable or malformed near-eye data; M5Stack specifies direct TX/RX alignment at no less than 30 cm and warns that shorter spacing causes abnormal reception.

validated_facts.fact: Firm blinks transfer measurable sub-degree-per-second impulses through a rigid glasses mount to the BMI270, but a two-blink detector is unsafe.
validated_facts.validation: Two retained 200 Hz captures. The original two-blink detector produced control-stage events; conservative four-impulse retuning replays both captures with zero stillness and head-motion sequences, while the harder intentional stage still recognizes only one sequence and remains NOT_PROVEN.

validated_facts.fact: The tested StickS3's original PTT project supports authenticated ArduinoOTA as sticks3-ptt.local, while bedside-countdown-s3 is a separate LilyGO T-Display-S3.
validated_facts.validation: Read-only inspection of the original PTT build script and firmware, live mDNS discovery of the separate bedside board, and saved hardware identities. Colibrino now preserves the PTT OTA credentials and hostname behind ignored configuration and a MAC-guarded uploader.

tasks.name: Separate StickS3 target
acceptance: Legacy AVR source remains untouched.
StickS3 has its own pinned PlatformIO environment.
A native host-test environment compiles sensor-independent logic.

tasks.name: Safe USB head-mouse prototype
acceptance: BMI270 data calibrates only while stationary.
Movement uses gyro rate with filtering, deadzone, fractional accumulation, and bounded HID reports.
The device emits no pointer movement until mouse mode is physically armed for two seconds.
Axis directions are verified on the glasses mount and head motion moves the host pointer.
A stationary armed control produces no spontaneous HID movement.

tasks.name: Onboard IR blink feasibility probe
acceptance: Transmit GPIO46 emits a controlled 38 kHz carrier envelope through RMT.
Receive GPIO42 captures raw demodulated pulse timing through RMT.
CDC logs retain timestamp, validity, symbol count, active time, total time, normalized ratio, and protocol stage.
The guided test measures open eye, closed eye, and repeated blinks without assuming signal polarity.
A pass requires at least 20 valid frames in each baseline, at least 4 sigma separation, at least 15 percent relative change, and at least two human-duration blink events.
Physical near-eye failure is retained as evidence and does not get relabeled as a capability.

tasks.name: External click-sensor boundary
acceptance: Blink classification consumes a sensor-neutral normalized sample.
A future analog TCRT5000 implementation can replace the onboard IR producer without changing USB click behavior.
No TCRT5000 purchase is recommended until the IMU-only sequence receives one repeat validation run.

tasks.name: StickS3 bench validation
acceptance: Firmware build completes without flashing as the pre-hardware gate.
StickS3 enumerates as both CDC and HID without spontaneous mouse reports.
Display reports BMI270 and stationary calibration succeeds.
Worn-device head motion moves the pointer with the expected axes.
High-rate stillness, deliberate-blink, and ordinary-head-motion CSV is retained outside Git.
The tightened IMU sequence passes two deliberate groups and produces zero control-stage events in a fresh run.

tasks.name: Generic ESP32-S3 simulator gate
acceptance: The portable production motion, optical blink-analysis, and IMU sequence sources cross-compile for a generic ESP32-S3 target.
Wokwi CLI lints the diagram and boots the firmware image.

The simulated firmware validates stationary gyro calibration, moving-calibration rejection, cursor deadzone, pointer direction and accumulation, invalid timestep rejection, optical separation, blink timing, the four-impulse IMU sequence, head-motion cancellation, and the complete guided feasibility protocol.
The run emits COLIBRINO_SIM_PASS and does not claim to validate unmodeled StickS3 peripherals or optics.

tasks.name: IMU-only blink gesture
acceptance: One through three temple impulses never recommend a click.
Four bounded impulses are required with 350 through 1100 milliseconds between adjacent impulses.
Pointer-scale rotation cancels partial state and suppresses detection for two quiet seconds.
A guided run records zero sequences during ordinary blinking, at least two during deliberate four-blink groups, and zero during head movement.
Runtime HID clicking remains disabled unless the complete current-boot guided run passes.

tasks.name: Authenticated StickS3 OTA
acceptance: Wi-Fi and ArduinoOTA compile only when the ignored device secrets header is available.
The service reuses the tested unit's established sticks3-ptt.local identity and authenticated password.
OTA start locks HID, releases mouse buttons, invalidates blink validation, cancels capture, and disables external 5 V before transfer.
The upload wrapper refuses any resolved device whose ARP MAC differs from AC:27:6E:D2:68:B8.
One cable flash installs the listener because the currently installed older Colibrino image has no OTA service.
After bootstrap, two authenticated OTA round trips succeed while the bedside-countdown-s3 remains untouched.

simulation_boundary.validated_in_wokwi: ESP32-S3 compilation and execution of sensor-independent motion, statistics, optical blink detection, four-impulse IMU detection, cancellation gates, and feasibility state-machine logic.
simulation_boundary.requires_sticks3_hardware: Regression of BMI270 mounting behavior, M5PM1 power control, display, buttons, composite TinyUSB CDC/HID, the IMU gesture across users and remounts, and any external click sensor.

sensor_purchase_decision.onboard_ir_pass: Do not use the integrated demodulating IR pair as a near-eye click sensor; its documented spacing and physical results reject that geometry.
sensor_purchase_decision.imu_retest: Repeat the guided four-blink run on the final rigid mount. Keep it only if at least two intentional sequences and zero ordinary-blink or head-motion sequences are recorded in repeated sessions.
sensor_purchase_decision.external_sensor_required: Use a separately bench-designed analog reflectance sensor such as TCRT5000 when the IMU gesture cannot pass consistently, is too tiring, or produces any control-stage event after conservative tuning.

remaining_hardware_questions: Does the four-blink BMI270 gesture remain separable after repeated removal and remounting of the glasses?
Is a four-blink click usable enough for the intended user, or only a proof that no external sensor is electrically required?
If an external analog sensor is needed, which expansion pins, supply rail, resistor values, and mechanical position meet electrical and eye-safety constraints?
When should the preserved original flash image be restored to the tested StickS3 after the remaining hardware run?
Does the first cable-bootstrap build advertise authenticated OTA as sticks3-ptt.local and complete two guarded round trips without affecting USB HID timing?
